intro: Runs on its own kind-inference cluster: agentgateway with the Gateway API Inference Extension, an InferencePool of two model-server replicas and the Endpoint Picker. No GPU: the replicas are llm-d simulators that publish real vLLM gauges with values we pin. The App tab shows those gauges live and where the gateway sent each request. Reset puts pool-a back to cold and pool-b to hot.

app.label: Inference pool, live
app.hint: Live KV cache, queue depth and routing for each replica.

1.title: The model pool
1.say: Two model-server replicas behind one InferencePool. The route points at the pool, not a Service, so the gateway asks the Endpoint Picker where each request goes.
1.point: pool-a starts cold (KV cache 10%, empty queue) and pool-b hot (90%, 8 waiting). Open the App tab to watch both.

blocks.title: The replicas, the route and their signals
blocks.instruction: List the two replicas, show that the HTTPRoute's backend is the InferencePool, and print the gauges each replica is pinned to.
blocks.expect: pool-a is cold and pool-b is hot, and the route's backend kind is InferencePool.

2.title: The Endpoint Picker (EPP)
2.say: Read the picker's scoring config straight off the cluster: three scorers with weights, and the pool's pointer to the picker.
2.point: Prefix-cache affinity counts most (×3); KV-cache use and queue depth break ties (×2 each).

blocks.title: How the picker scores
blocks.instruction: Print the EndpointPickerConfig and the InferencePool's endpointPickerRef.
blocks.expect: Queue and KV-cache scorers at weight 2, prefix-cache at weight 3, and the pool wired to vllm-sim-epp.

3.title: KV-cache-aware routing
3.say: Send eight requests while pool-b's cache is nearly full, then swap the gauges and send eight more.
3.point: Nothing about the route changes. The picker re-scores on the new gauges and the traffic follows. Watch the App tab while the second step runs.

blocks.title: Traffic avoids the full cache
blocks.instruction: Print the signals, then send eight requests and count which replica served them from the gateway's access log.
blocks.expect: All eight go to pool-a, the replica with free cache.

blocks.title: Flip it on cue
blocks.instruction: Saturate pool-a (95% cache, 9 waiting) and free pool-b, give the picker a moment to re-scrape, then send eight more.
blocks.expect: The traffic moves: all eight go to pool-b.

4.title: Queue-aware routing
4.say: Give both replicas the same cache, but back pool-a's queue up to 30 waiting.
4.point: The queue scorer steers around the head-of-line-blocked replica. This is what keeps tail latency down.

blocks.title: Traffic avoids the long queue
blocks.instruction: Pin both replicas at 50% cache, give pool-a 30 queued requests, then send eight.
blocks.expect: All eight go to pool-b, the replica that can start work now.

5.title: Prefix-cache affinity
5.say: The highest-weighted scorer: keep requests that share a prompt prefix on the replica that already holds it.
5.point: Reusing a cached prefix skips prefill, the biggest latency win in serving. KV and queue then break ties and steer around saturation.

6.title: Serving priority with InferenceObjective
6.say: Two priority tiers on the pool. Each request names its tier in a header.
6.point: Priority only bites when the pool is saturated: interactive work is dispatched before batch. On an idle pool both come straight back.

blocks.title: Tiers on the pool, one per request
blocks.instruction: List the InferenceObjectives, then send one request as interactive and one as batch.
blocks.expect: interactive is priority 10 and batch priority 0, and both requests return 200 on the idle pool.
